sentences.en: They went past the warehouses where the merchants kept the goods meant to be loaded into ships.
sentences.zh: 他们经过了商人存放要装船的货物的仓库。

picturePages.text: In one warehouse, labourers were unloading bags of pepper and coriander seeds. In another, they were stacking up bales of cotton cloth woven in bright

sentences.en: In one warehouse, labourers were unloading bags of pepper and coriander seeds.
sentences.zh: 在一间仓库里，工人们正在卸下一袋袋胡椒和香菜种子。

sentences.en: In another, they were stacking up bales of cotton cloth woven in bright
sentences.zh: 在另一个房间里，他们正在堆放一捆捆用亮色编织而成的棉布。

picturePages.text: Three ships stood anchored at the jetty, tied to the shore by thick ropes. Two more ships were waiting out at sea. Small boats were moving in and out among them with the boatmen selling everything from flowers and fruits to beads and woodcarvings.

sentences.en: Three ships stood anchored at the jetty, tied to the shore by thick ropes.
sentences.zh: 三艘船停泊在码头上，用粗绳子绑在岸上。

sentences.en: Two more ships were waiting out at sea.
sentences.zh: 还有两艘船在海上等待。

sentences.en: Small boats were moving in and out among them with the boatmen selling everything from flowers and fruits to beads and woodcarvings.
sentences.zh: 小船在他们中间进进出出，船夫们兜售着各种东西，从鲜花、水果到珠子、木雕。

picturePages.text: Among the ships anchored at the jetty was the ship with the black and green sails that they had seen in the morning. They went towards a ship that was being loaded with goods. As they neared it, a soldier carrying a spear stopped them.

sentences.en: Among the ships anchored at the jetty was the ship with the black and green sails that they had seen in the morning.
sentences.zh: 停泊在码头的船只之中，就有他们早上看到的那艘黑绿风帆的船。

sentences.en: They went towards a ship that was being loaded with goods.
sentences.zh: 他们走向一艘正在装载货物的船。

sentences.en: As they neared it, a soldier carrying a spear stopped them.
sentences.zh: 当他们接近时，一名手持长矛的士兵拦住了他们。

picturePages.text: “Halt! Watch where you are going!” the man yelled.

sentences.en: “Halt!
sentences.zh: “站住！

sentences.en: Watch where you are going!”
sentences.zh: 看你往哪儿走！”

sentences.en: the man yelled.
sentences.zh: 男人喊道。

picturePages.text: “No one is allowed on this ship without a royal permit.” “Permit?” Sundari looked puzzled. “Why?” “Because it is a royal ship, you silly girl!”

sentences.en: “No one is allowed on this ship without a royal permit.”
sentences.zh: “未经皇家许可，任何人不得登上这艘船。”

sentences.en: “Permit?”
sentences.zh: “允许？”

sentences.en: Sundari looked puzzled.
sentences.zh: 孙达里一脸困惑。

sentences.en: “Why?”
sentences.zh: “为什么？”

sentences.en: “Because it is a royal ship, you silly girl!”
sentences.zh: “因为这是皇家船啊，你这个傻丫头！”

picturePages.text: “You mean this ship belongs to the royal navy?” Basava’s eyes widened in surprise. “Are we going to war?” “Of course not! This is a trading ship.

sentences.en: “You mean this ship belongs to the royal navy?”
sentences.zh: “你是说这艘船属于皇家海军？”

sentences.en: Basava’s eyes widened in surprise.
sentences.zh: 巴萨瓦惊讶地睁大了眼睛。

sentences.en: “Are we going to war?”
sentences.zh: “我们要打仗吗？”

sentences.en: “Of course not!
sentences.zh: “当然不是！

sentences.en: This is a trading ship.
sentences.zh: 这是一艘贸易船。

picturePages.text: His Majesty King Narasimha Varman owns many ships that trade with far off kingdoms. This one is going to the port of Tamralipti in the north.” “We are looking for a ship that has come from the kingdom of Kamboja … ” Sundari began hesitantly.

sentences.en: His Majesty King Narasimha Varman owns many ships that trade with far off kingdoms.
sentences.zh: 纳拉辛哈·瓦尔曼 (Narasimha Varman) 国王陛下拥有许多与遥远王国进行贸易的船只。

sentences.en: This one is going to the port of Tamralipti in the north.”
sentences.zh: 这艘船将前往北部的塔姆拉利普蒂 (Tamralipti) 港口。”

sentences.en: “We are looking for a ship that has come from the kingdom of Kamboja … ” Sundari began hesitantly.
sentences.zh: “我们正在寻找一艘来自坎博贾王国的船只……”桑达里犹豫着说道。

picturePages.text: “Our father is a sailor and he sailed for Kamboja many months ago. We want to ask the sailors if they have seen his ship.” “Kamboja?” the soldier asked.

sentences.en: “Our father is a sailor and he sailed for Kamboja many months ago.
sentences.zh: “我们的父亲是一名水手，几个月前他航行到坎博贾。

sentences.en: We want to ask the sailors if they have seen his ship.”
sentences.zh: 我们想问问水手们是否见过他的船。”

sentences.en: “Kamboja?”
sentences.zh: “坎博贾？”

sentences.en: the soldier asked.
sentences.zh: 士兵问道。

picturePages.text: He then pointed to the ship with the black and green sails and said, “That ship’s arrived from there.”

sentences.en: He then pointed to the ship with the black and green sails and said, “That ship’s arrived from there.”
sentences.zh: 然后他指着那艘黑绿风帆的船说道：“那艘船是从那里来的。”

picturePages.text: Basava and Sundari ran to the ship, up the gangplank and on to its deck. They stopped when they saw that all the sailors on board were foreigners. They were speaking to each other in a strange tongue! “Oh no!” Basava sighed.

sentences.en: Basava and Sundari ran to the ship, up the gangplank and on to its deck.
sentences.zh: 巴萨瓦和桑达里跑向船，爬上跳板，跑到甲板上。

sentences.en: They stopped when they saw that all the sailors on board were foreigners.
sentences.zh: 当他们看到船上的水手都是外国人时，他们停了下来。

sentences.en: They were speaking to each other in a strange tongue!
sentences.zh: 他们用一种奇怪的语言互相交谈！

sentences.en: “Oh no!”
sentences.zh: “哦不！”

sentences.en: Basava sighed.
sentences.zh: 巴萨瓦叹了口气。

picturePages.text: “How do we make them understand us?” “Easy!” Sundari grinned.

sentences.en: “How do we make them understand us?”
sentences.zh: “我们如何让他们理解我们？”

sentences.en: “Easy!”
sentences.zh: “简单的！”

sentences.en: Sundari grinned.
sentences.zh: 桑达里笑了。

picturePages.text: “We talk to them like Amma does when they come to buy vegetables.” “Of course!” laughed Basava, “We act and make signs with our hands.” They looked around trying to spot a sailor with a friendly face.

sentences.en: “We talk to them like Amma does when they come to buy vegetables.”
sentences.zh: “我们和他们交谈，就像他们来买菜时妈妈所做的那样。”

sentences.en: “Of course!”
sentences.zh: “当然！”

sentences.en: laughed Basava, “We act and make signs with our hands.”
sentences.zh: 巴萨瓦笑道：“我们用手行动、做手势。”

sentences.en: They looked around trying to spot a sailor with a friendly face.
sentences.zh: 他们环顾四周，试图找到一位面容友善的水手。

picturePages.text: Finally, they went up to a sailor sitting on a roll of rope.

sentences.en: Finally, they went up to a sailor sitting on a roll of rope.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们走到了一个坐在绳子上的水手面前。

picturePages.text: He was an old man with a dark, leathery, sunburnt face. There were deep lines around his narrow eyes. He wore loose pyjamas, a sleeveless jacket, bright bangles and earrings. “Kamboja?” Sundari asked nervously.

sentences.en: He was an old man with a dark, leathery, sunburnt face.
sentences.zh: 他是一位老人，脸色黝黑，皮肤黝黑，被晒伤了。

sentences.en: There were deep lines around his narrow eyes.
sentences.zh: 他狭长的眼睛周围有深深的皱纹。

sentences.en: He wore loose pyjamas, a sleeveless jacket, bright bangles and earrings.
sentences.zh: 他穿着宽松的睡衣、无袖夹克、戴着明亮的手镯和耳环。

sentences.en: “Kamboja?”
sentences.zh: “坎博贾？”

sentences.en: Sundari asked nervously.
sentences.zh: 孙达里紧张地问道。

picturePages.text: The man nodded happily, “Kamboja!” Basava pointed to the sail, then he pointed to the red skirt Sundari was wearing and said, “Ship? Red sail?”

sentences.en: The man nodded happily, “Kamboja!”
sentences.zh: 那人高兴地点点头：“坎博贾！”

sentences.en: Basava pointed to the sail, then he pointed to the red skirt Sundari was wearing and said, “Ship?
sentences.zh: 巴萨瓦指着船帆，又指着桑达里穿着的红裙说道：“船？

sentences.en: Red sail?”
sentences.zh: 红帆？”

picturePages.text: The man frowned and shook his head. Sundari tried to explain. She tapped the side of the ship and said, “Ship?” Then she pointed to the sails and to her skirt, “Sail? Red?”

sentences.en: The man frowned and shook his head.
sentences.zh: 男人皱起眉头，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: Sundari tried to explain.
sentences.zh: 桑达里试图解释。

sentences.en: She tapped the side of the ship and said, “Ship?”
sentences.zh: 她敲了敲船舷，道：“船？”

sentences.en: Then she pointed to the sails and to her skirt, “Sail?
sentences.zh: 然后她指着船帆和裙子，“船帆？

sentences.en: Red?”
sentences.zh: 红色？”

picturePages.text: The man pointed to the sea and said something in his own language. “Yes! A ship with red sails. Have you seen it?” Sundari asked excitedly.

sentences.en: The man pointed to the sea and said something in his own language.
sentences.zh: 男人指着大海，用自己的语言说了些什么。

sentences.en: “Yes!
sentences.zh: “是啊！

sentences.en: A ship with red sails.
sentences.zh: 一艘挂着红帆的船。

sentences.en: Have you seen it?”
sentences.zh: 你见过吗？

sentences.en: Sundari asked excitedly.
sentences.zh: 孙达里兴奋地问道。

picturePages.text: The man looked a bit puzzled. “Our father … Appa!” Sundari was acting out a tall man with a moustache. “Oh!” The man then flapped his arms to mimic a bird flying.

sentences.en: The man looked a bit puzzled.
sentences.zh: 男人显得有些疑惑。

sentences.en: “Our father … Appa!”
sentences.zh: “我们的父亲……阿帕！”

sentences.en: Sundari was acting out a tall man with a moustache.
sentences.zh: 桑达里扮演的是一个留着小胡子的高个子男人。

sentences.en: “Oh!”
The man then flapped his arms to mimic a bird flying.
sentences.zh: 然后，该男子挥动手臂，模仿一只鸟飞翔的样子。

picturePages.text: “YES!” the children jumped and yelled in delight, “A flying eagle is on the sail!” The man was laughing as he stood up and pulled them by their hands to the other end of the ship.

sentences.en: “YES!”
sentences.zh: “是的！”

sentences.en: the children jumped and yelled in delight, “A flying eagle is on the sail!”
sentences.zh: 孩子们跳了起来，高兴地喊着：“一只飞翔的雄鹰扬帆起航了！”

sentences.en: The man was laughing as he stood up and pulled them by their hands to the other end of the ship.
sentences.zh: 那人笑着站起来，拉着他们的手往船的另一端走去。

picturePages.text: Then he pointed to the horizon where a ship was slowly sailing towards them, its red sails blowing proudly in the breeze.

sentences.en: Then he pointed to the horizon where a ship was slowly sailing towards them, its red sails blowing proudly in the breeze.
sentences.zh: 然后他指了指天边，一艘船正缓缓驶向他们，红色的风帆在微风中傲然飘扬。

picturePages.text: Basava and Sundari were speechless! There, before their eyes, were the familiar high masts, the curving prow, the red sails with flying eagles... “Your Appa is a sailor?” the man asked gently, looking at their delighted faces. “Is he on that ship?”

sentences.en: Basava and Sundari were speechless!
sentences.zh: 巴萨瓦和桑达里都无语了！

sentences.en: There, before their eyes, were the familiar high masts, the curving prow, the red sails with flying eagles...
sentences.zh: 眼前，是熟悉的高高的桅杆，弯曲的船头，飞翔的雄鹰的红帆……

sentences.en: “Your Appa is a sailor?”
sentences.zh: “你的阿帕是一名水手？”

sentences.en: the man asked gently, looking at their delighted faces.
sentences.zh: 男人看着他们一脸欣喜的表情，轻声问道。

sentences.en: “Is he on that ship?”
sentences.zh: “他在那艘船上吗？”

picturePages.text: “Oh!” The children stared at him in disbelief. “You can speak our language!” Sundari exclaimed.

sentences.en: “Oh!”
The children stared at him in disbelief.
sentences.zh: 孩子们难以置信地看着他。

sentences.en: “You can speak our language!”
sentences.zh: “你会说我们的语言！”

sentences.en: Sundari exclaimed.
sentences.zh: 孙达里惊呼道。

picturePages.text: “A little bit,” the man laughed. “I come to Mamallapuram often. But I did enjoy your acting, especially ‘the tall man with the moustache’ part!”

sentences.en: “A little bit,” the man laughed.
sentences.zh: “有一点。”男人笑道。

sentences.en: “I come to Mamallapuram often.
sentences.zh: “我经常来马马拉普拉姆。

sentences.en: But I did enjoy your acting, especially ‘the tall man with the moustache’ part!”
sentences.zh: 但我确实很喜欢你的表演，尤其是‘留着小胡子的高个子男人’的部分！”

sentences.zh: 巴萨瓦和桑达里站在码头上，高兴地等待船回家，教了他们的水手朋友许多新单词。

picturePages.text: 3. What did children study in school in the Pallava times? The subjects included logic, law, mathematics, grammar, astronomy, philosophy, the Vedas, economics and politics. 4. Women, especially of noble families, were educated, but were not allowed to study the Vedas. 5.

stories.title: Greenfield: Building a City
stories.synopsis: 许多真实玩家一起，把方块变成了一座城市。
paragraphs: Greenfield is a city inside Minecraft. It is a building project made by a team of real players. The team takes ideas from Los Angeles and the west coast of America. Their aim is a city that looks like a place where people could really live.

The project's official wiki describes a team of more than 150 people. It lists districts, landmarks, buildings, and transport. A city is more than one beautiful building. It is many places connected together. This makes a city project different from building one house.
A team project raises interesting questions. If your building looks wonderful alone, will it fit beside someone else's building? Who decides where a road should go?

Imagine joining a city-building team. What would you add first: a harbor, a school, a park, or a station? How would your choice help other parts of the city? A shared world invites you to think about both your own idea and the needs of others.

stories.title: Chipko takes root
stories.synopsis: 洪水改变了女孩的生活。她和村民怎样守护森林？
paragraphs: Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom! High up in the branches of her tree, Dichi plays on her dholak.

Her three brothers clamber up the same sturdy tree while their sheep jostle and bleat on the meadow below. “Dichi!” echoes Dada’s voice through the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. “Come. We must visit your grandmother across the river.
Boys, bring the sheep home safely.”
“Can’t we come too?” begs Shyam. “Next time,” says Dada firmly. “Dichi will stay on there to nurse Grandma. She is very sick now.”

Dada guides their mule through knee-deep river water. Nimble as a mountain goat, Dichi tucks her skirt to skip on the rocks. Her toes tingle in the chill waters, until she slips and tumbles in with a splash. “Careful!” warns Chacha, who is fishing nearby.
In a sudden surge, the river swells and roars about them in a furious flash flood. Chacha rushes over to grab Dichi by the arms.

Her left leg is caught beneath a rolling boulder. Dada’s figure is a blur – his voice muffled by the raging waters. Caught in the current, the mule swims and staggers to the other side, its burden toppled and swept away.
Chacha can barely keep his balance in the deluge, as he tries to extricate Dichi’s leg from below the obstinate rock. Drenched in muddy water, he musters all his strength to yank Dichi out.
His powerful shoulders carry her back to Ma who crouches, sobbing over her bedraggled daughter. Sharp needles of pain shoot up Dichi’s left leg.
Enveloped by a fit of trembling, she faints.
Leaving Dichi with her horrified Ma, Chacha charges back for Dada. But Dada never returns. Cold fingers of fear clutch at Dichi’s heart when they bring his body home from the river.
Dichi hears of the sports goods company that felled their chir, pine, deodar and ash trees to make cricket bats and other sports stuff.

Why do they chop our forests? Can’t they see the landslides thunder down the mountainside? The fierce flash floods that carry away the poor folk? Those floods took her Dada...and the power in Dichi’s left leg.
She now has no sensation in it below the knee.
Can Dichi ever forget those icy river waters? She still feels them block her ears, leak into her nose, blur her eyes and close over her head.

But no. Chacha says she must think of the good things...dwell on the positive. Courage wells up with a glowing warmth that melts away her fears. She still has Ma and her brothers. Chacha and Chachi care for all of them.
They have no children of their own.

Dichi loves her Chacha like her own Dada, but is upset when she overhears Chachi say to Ma, “Your brother is a good man. But his gambling is a habit that can make or break you – and now we’re going downhill...”
‘Chacha – a gambler? Oh no! It can’t be so!’ Days pass.
Dichi and her family fall into a new routine.

Dichi sits on her ash tree glancing down at the two rugged crutches that lie on the grass below... Chacha made them for her from her mighty ash. “My branches are thin and fat, long and short,” whispers her ash, “but I’m strong.”
Dichi climbs higher to peer into a bird’s nest.

She trails her fingers after a row of ants, and sniffs the cool scent of ash leaves. ‘You’re MY ash tree. Chacha says I’m just like you, sturdy as a yak. With these crutches, I’ll be strong and fierce as a Yeti.’

“Hey Dichi! Everyone’s at the meeting!” yells Shyam. Quick as lightning, Dichi slides down, picks up her crutches and follows him to the vast shady tree where the villagers gather around Gauri, the village elder.
“We may be illiterate, but we are wise folk,” says Gauri. “We will not allow them to auction our precious trees to any company.
When Chand, the contractor comes with his axemen, we will go out into the forests and hug the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. There will be no violence.”

The villagers troop into the forest chanting their Chipko slogans. Dichi grabs her dholak to boom along with the chant of children who bounce around like rubber balls. Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka!
Dhoom!
“What do these forests bear?” shouts Dichi. “Soil, water and pure air,” chorus the children, following her with a hop and a jump.

But a cluster of uniformed axemen is there before them. Contractor Chand’s bulky form looms above, barking out orders to methodically mark the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees for auction with a chalky white X. The villagers clamour around them in fury.
They bear down upon the axemen. They brandish their dholaks filling the forest with Chipko songs.
“Let us protect and plant the trees, Go awaken the villages and drive away the axemen.”
Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom!
Contractor Chand gives an evil grin as he and his axemen troop into a bus and drive away. The next day, there is a hubbub as the village men get ready for a long drive down the mountainside.

Trucks are sent by the government for the menfolk to view the film – a sudden treat that can’t be ignored, as movies are rarely seen in these parts. The women are busy weaving. The village school is abuzz.
Children learn new Chipko slogans, draw chir, pine, deodar and ash trees on their slates, beat on their dholaks and dance.
“Soil ours, water ours, ours are these forests too, Our forefathers raised these, it is we who must protect these too.” Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom!
After school, Dichi and her brothers take the sheep into the forest to graze. Along with the other village kids, they hug the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees.
Their cheerful voices fade as the sun dips into the horizon and the children head back to the village with bundles of firewood on their heads.
Dichi lingers to close her eyes and lean on her favourite tree. Its feathery leaves calm her, the smooth bark cools her cheeks as it seems to whisper to her.
‘No one must take away my ash!’ thinks Dichi firmly. Time stands still. All is right with the world.

But these tranquil trees are all aflutter when from their bosom parrots squawk and take wing in a flurry of green feathers. Squirrels burst out of the undergrowth in a frenzy. With a screech of brakes, a bus jolts to a stop beneath the cliff.
Spattered with mud, it is enveloped in a cloud of dust.

Dichi peers through the curtain of leaves. Men troop out in single file. Their khaki uniforms are scruffy, their axes glint as they head towards her forest with its chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. Burly Chand follows. Their footsteps echo down the mountainside. ‘Help!
My ash!
They can’t cut my ash!’ Dichi slips off the branch to slither down the steep mountainside. Panting, she throws her crutches over the gentle slope of green, to roll after them.
Rumble, tumble, thump! Rumble tumble thump! Dichi’s heart booms like her dholak. Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka!

Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom! ‘I need help!’ Dichi flounders, gropes for her crutches and totters home. “Ma!” she gasps. Ma rushes out to wrap protective arms about her as she crumbles like charred wood in a bonfire.
“Ma! My ash! The – the – They’re –– cutting it!” “Who, child? Talk slowly.
Here – drink this water.” “They c–came in a big bus with axes! So many men. Huge men with sharp axes, Ma!” “Oh no!
It’s the contractor’s men come to chop our trees! Quick! We have to do something.” “You wait here.

I’ll gather everyone,” says Dichi catching her breath and squaring her shoulders. Women and children rush to rally around with dholaks. “We’ve got to do something. Contractor Chand tricked our menfolk into going away!” Ma says, wringing the edge of her phantu.
“How do we stop them without our menfolk?” “We’ll show them!
But remember – absolutely no violence,” says the village elder, Gauri who is Ma’s best friend. Dichi’s heart booms along with her dholak.
Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom! “Chipko!”
she yells. “Hug the trees!” holler the women and children till their throats ache for a drink of hot buttered tea.
The forest throbs with the wails of chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. “What do the forests bear?” shouts Dichi, raising her fist high. “Soil, water and pure air!” chorus the women and children.
The X that marks every tree to be cut, feels like a gash – a wound that will never heal. My Ash!

What will I do without you? Dichi’s trembling fingers scratch at the bark to erase the X. “You can’t cut my ash,” she says fiercely, her arms wrapped around her tree. “Move out,” rasps Contractor Chand, pulling her away roughly.
Dichi whirls to stamp her feet. Her eagle eyes scrutinize the axemen who crowd around. They look tired and wary.
As her gaze fixes on one figure hiding behind a tree, his eyes drop to the ground. Dichi’s eyes widen, “Chacha – you too?”
There’s a hush in the woods. Chacha slumps to drop his axe with a clink. “I have a gambling debt. I am out of work...” says Chacha lamely.
Dichi and her brothers rush to hug him.
“Chacha, we’ll work and help you repay your debts! I can weave a shawl and sell it!” says Dichi. “I’ll work at the soap unit,” says Ram. “I’ll work at the water mill!”
says Shyam. Chacha’s head droops, a teardrop glistens in his eye. He throws off the shirt of his uniform, picks up Dichi’s dholak. Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka!
Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom!
“What do the forests bear?” boom Chacha and Dichi. “Soil, water and pure air!” chorus the women and children.
“You foolish girl! These forests bear timber, resin and foreign exchange!” cuts in Contractor Chand. “MEN, chop down those trees at once! Every one of them – chir, pine, deodar and ash!”
“No! No! No! Pleeeease don’t!” says Dichi holding on to her tree.
“The trees are our saviours!” “She’s right,” says Chacha. “She lost her Dada in that flood.”
An axeman opens burning palms to drop his axe. Another axe clinks down and another... until one by one the axemen troop out of the forest.
Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom! “Chipko!

Hug the trees!” cries Dichi. Hoarse voices echo with the wind that whines through the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. “Cut this forest and you’ll wipe out our village,” says Ma. A bulky form blots out the sky.
Contractor Chand towers before them, looking like thunder.
Shaking an angry fist, he stamps his feet, turns on his heel and marches away.
Squeezing her hands together, Dichi takes a deep breath. She can’t believe it – all the axemen have gone! “We did it!” says Ma. “We’ll take our Chipko Movement to every part of India.”
“Chipko! Hug the trees!” cry the women and children. Toes tap, feet thump. Hand in hand, they swing into a joyous victory dance.

The ash sways in the breeze. Dichi rests her cheek against its cool bark. She feels its feathery leaves rustle in the evening breeze. “I’m like you, strong and fierce like a Yeti...sturdy as a yak,” Dichi whispers to her ash tree.
Glossary Chacha - Uncle Chipko - To stick to, hug Dada - Father Dholak - Drum Ma - Mother Phantu - Bhotiya tribal women wear this shawl on the head tucked behind to make two pockets.
Yak - Long-haired domestic cattle Yeti - An imaginary giant ape or an abominable snowman believed to live in the Himalaya mountains of Nepal and Tibet.

“Forestry is not about trees. It is about people.” - Jack Westoby, author of The Purpose of Forests • The Bhotiya tribe live high in the Himalaya mountains of India.

They love and protect the forests because they depend on them for firewood, tools and building houses. • In 1970 floods occur in Alaknanda when the forests are cleared, sweeping away houses, bridges, cattle and thousands of people.
The Bhotiyas know they have to save their forests so they adopt the Chipko Movement which promotes non-violence.
An illiterate woman, Gaura Devi, a tribal leader from Chamoli District, mobilizes the women of her region to protect their forests.

Some consider this an eco-feminist movement where women are actively involved. • In the Alaknanda Valley, Chandi Prasad Bhatt is a humble social worker who teaches the people to embrace the trees and save them from the axemen.

Like Mahatma Gandhi, he doesn’t use violence. He encourages tribals to develop their local industries without disturbing the forest wealth. • “Ecology is permanent economy,” says Chipko leader, Sunderlal Bahuguna, who continues the movement to fight the felling of forests.
• Like Dichi in this book, a little Bhotiya girl spots the axemen and alerts the village women who march into the forest with shouts of Chipko slogans.
Without violence, they block the axemen from cutting the trees. • In 1980, the Government of India passes a law to protect these forests.
This is one of the first important environmental movements in India.

sentences.zh: 当承包商昌德带着他的斧头手来时，我们将走进森林，拥抱奇尔树、松树、雪松树和白蜡树。

sentences.en: There will be no violence.”
sentences.zh: 不会有暴力。”

picturePages.text: The villagers troop into the forest chanting their Chipko slogans. Dichi grabs her dholak to boom along with the chant of children who bounce around like rubber balls. Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka!

sentences.en: The villagers troop into the forest chanting their Chipko slogans.
sentences.zh: 村民们高呼奇普科口号，成群结队地走进森林。

sentences.en: Dichi grabs her dholak to boom along with the chant of children who bounce around like rubber balls.
sentences.zh: 迪奇抓住她的多拉克，伴随着像橡皮球一样弹跳的孩子们的歌声。

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

picturePages.text: Dhoom!

sentences.en: Dhoom!
sentences.zh: 哎哟！

picturePages.text: “What do these forests bear?” shouts Dichi. “Soil, water and pure air,” chorus the children, following her with a hop and a jump.

sentences.en: “What do these forests bear?”
sentences.zh: “这些森林里有什么？”

sentences.en: shouts Dichi.
sentences.zh: 迪奇喊道。

sentences.en: “Soil, water and pure air,” chorus the children, following her with a hop and a jump.
sentences.zh: “土壤、水和纯净的空气。”孩子们跟着她一蹦一跳地合唱。

picturePages.text: But a cluster of uniformed axemen is there before them. Contractor Chand’s bulky form looms above, barking out orders to methodically mark the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees for auction with a chalky white X. The villagers clamour around them in fury.

sentences.en: But a cluster of uniformed axemen is there before them.
sentences.zh: 但在他们面前有一群穿着制服的斧兵。

sentences.en: Contractor Chand’s bulky form looms above, barking out orders to methodically mark the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees for auction with a chalky white X.
sentences.zh: 承包商昌德庞大的身躯赫然出现在上方，大声发出命令，用粉笔状的白色“X”有条不紊地标记待拍卖的冷杉树、松树、雪松树和白蜡树。

sentences.en: The villagers clamour around them in fury.
sentences.zh: 周围的村民愤怒地叫嚷着。

picturePages.text: They bear down upon the axemen. They brandish their dholaks filling the forest with Chipko songs.

sentences.en: They bear down upon the axemen.
sentences.zh: 他们向斧兵猛冲过来。

sentences.en: They brandish their dholaks filling the forest with Chipko songs.
sentences.zh: 他们挥舞着多拉克，森林里充满奇普科歌曲。

picturePages.text: “Let us protect and plant the trees, Go awaken the villages and drive away the axemen.”

sentences.en: “Let us protect and plant the trees, Go awaken the villages and drive away the axemen.”
sentences.zh: “让我们保护树木，植树造林，去唤醒村庄，赶走斧兵。”

picturePages.text: Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom!

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom!
sentences.zh: 哎哟！

picturePages.text: Contractor Chand gives an evil grin as he and his axemen troop into a bus and drive away. The next day, there is a hubbub as the village men get ready for a long drive down the mountainside.

sentences.en: Contractor Chand gives an evil grin as he and his axemen troop into a bus and drive away.
sentences.zh: 承包商昌德邪恶地一笑，和他的斧头手们坐上一辆公共汽车开走了。

sentences.en: The next day, there is a hubbub as the village men get ready for a long drive down the mountainside.
sentences.zh: 第二天，村里的男人们准备长途驾车下山，周围一片喧闹。

picturePages.text: Trucks are sent by the government for the menfolk to view the film – a sudden treat that can’t be ignored, as movies are rarely seen in these parts. The women are busy weaving. The village school is abuzz.

sentences.en: Trucks are sent by the government for the menfolk to view the film – a sudden treat that can’t be ignored, as movies are rarely seen in these parts.
sentences.zh: 政府派出卡车让男人们观看这部电影——这是一种不可忽视的突然享受，因为这些地方很少看电影。

sentences.en: The women are busy weaving.
sentences.zh: 妇女们正忙着织布。

sentences.en: The village school is abuzz.
sentences.zh: 村里的学校热闹非凡。

picturePages.text: Children learn new Chipko slogans, draw chir, pine, deodar and ash trees on their slates, beat on their dholaks and dance.

sentences.en: Children learn new Chipko slogans, draw chir, pine, deodar and ash trees on their slates, beat on their dholaks and dance.
sentences.zh: 孩子们学习新的 Chipko 口号，在石板上画出奇普科树、松树、雪松树和白蜡树，敲打 Dholak 并跳舞。

picturePages.text: “Soil ours, water ours, ours are these forests too, Our forefathers raised these, it is we who must protect these too.” Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom!

sentences.en: “Soil ours, water ours, ours are these forests too, Our forefathers raised these, it is we who must protect these too.”
sentences.zh: “土壤是我们的，水是我们的，这些森林也是我们的，我们的祖先养育了这些，我们也必须保护这些。”

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom!
sentences.zh: 哎哟！

picturePages.text: After school, Dichi and her brothers take the sheep into the forest to graze. Along with the other village kids, they hug the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees.

sentences.en: After school, Dichi and her brothers take the sheep into the forest to graze.
sentences.zh: 放学后，迪奇和她的兄弟们带着羊到森林里吃草。

sentences.en: Along with the other village kids, they hug the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees.
sentences.zh: 他们和其他村里的孩子一起拥抱奇树、松树、雪松树和白蜡树。

picturePages.text: Their cheerful voices fade as the sun dips into the horizon and the children head back to the village with bundles of firewood on their heads.

sentences.en: Their cheerful voices fade as the sun dips into the horizon and the children head back to the village with bundles of firewood on their heads.
sentences.zh: 当太阳落入地平线时，他们欢快的声音逐渐消失，孩子们头顶着柴火返回村庄。

picturePages.text: Dichi lingers to close her eyes and lean on her favourite tree. Its feathery leaves calm her, the smooth bark cools her cheeks as it seems to whisper to her.

sentences.en: Dichi lingers to close her eyes and lean on her favourite tree.
sentences.zh: 迪奇闭上眼睛，靠在她最喜欢的树上。

sentences.en: Its feathery leaves calm her, the smooth bark cools her cheeks as it seems to whisper to her.
sentences.zh: 它的羽毛状叶子让她平静下来，光滑的树皮让她的脸颊凉爽，仿佛在对她低语。

picturePages.text: ‘No one must take away my ash!’ thinks Dichi firmly. Time stands still. All is right with the world.

sentences.en: ‘No one must take away my ash!’ thinks Dichi firmly.
sentences.zh: “任何人都不能拿走我的骨灰！”迪奇坚定地想。

sentences.en: Time stands still.
sentences.zh: 时间静止了。

sentences.en: All is right with the world.
sentences.zh: 世界一切都好。

picturePages.text: But these tranquil trees are all aflutter when from their bosom parrots squawk and take wing in a flurry of green feathers. Squirrels burst out of the undergrowth in a frenzy. With a screech of brakes, a bus jolts to a stop beneath the cliff.

sentences.en: But these tranquil trees are all aflutter when from their bosom parrots squawk and take wing in a flurry of green feathers.
sentences.zh: 但当鹦鹉从它们的怀里发出嘎嘎叫声，并在绿色的羽毛中展翅飞翔时，这些宁静的树木都在颤动。

sentences.en: Squirrels burst out of the undergrowth in a frenzy.
sentences.zh: 松鼠疯狂地从灌木丛中冲出来。

sentences.en: With a screech of brakes, a bus jolts to a stop beneath the cliff.
sentences.zh: 随着一阵刺耳的刹车声，一辆公共汽车颠簸停在悬崖下。

picturePages.text: Spattered with mud, it is enveloped in a cloud of dust.

sentences.en: Spattered with mud, it is enveloped in a cloud of dust.
sentences.zh: 它溅满了泥土，笼罩在一片尘土之中。

picturePages.text: Dichi peers through the curtain of leaves. Men troop out in single file. Their khaki uniforms are scruffy, their axes glint as they head towards her forest with its chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. Burly Chand follows. Their footsteps echo down the mountainside. ‘Help!

sentences.en: Dichi peers through the curtain of leaves.
sentences.zh: 迪奇透过树叶的帘子往外看。

sentences.en: Men troop out in single file.
sentences.zh: 男人们排成一列。

sentences.en: Their khaki uniforms are scruffy, their axes glint as they head towards her forest with its chir, pine, deodar and ash trees.
sentences.zh: 他们的卡其色制服破烂不堪，当他们走向她的森林时，斧头闪闪发光，那里长满了松树、雪松树和白蜡树。

sentences.en: Burly Chand follows.
sentences.zh: 魁梧的昌德紧随其后。

sentences.en: Their footsteps echo down the mountainside. ‘Help!
sentences.zh: 他们的脚步声在山腰下回响。 '帮助！

picturePages.text: My ash!

sentences.en: My ash!
sentences.zh: 我的灰！

picturePages.text: They can’t cut my ash!’ Dichi slips off the branch to slither down the steep mountainside. Panting, she throws her crutches over the gentle slope of green, to roll after them.

sentences.en: They can’t cut my ash!’ Dichi slips off the branch to slither down the steep mountainside.
sentences.zh: 他们砍不了我的骨灰！”迪奇从树枝上滑下来，滑下陡峭的山坡。

sentences.en: Panting, she throws her crutches over the gentle slope of green, to roll after them.
sentences.zh: 她气喘吁吁地把拐杖扔到绿色的缓坡上，跟在他们后面滚动。

picturePages.text: Rumble, tumble, thump! Rumble tumble thump! Dichi’s heart booms like her dholak. Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka!

sentences.en: Rumble, tumble, thump!
sentences.zh: 轰隆隆、翻滚、扑通！

sentences.en: Rumble tumble thump!
sentences.zh: 轰隆隆扑通扑通！

sentences.en: Dichi’s heart booms like her dholak.
sentences.zh: 迪奇的心像她的多拉克一样剧烈跳动。

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

picturePages.text: Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom! ‘I need help!’ Dichi flounders, gropes for her crutches and totters home. “Ma!” she gasps. Ma rushes out to wrap protective arms about her as she crumbles like charred wood in a bonfire.

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom! ‘I need help!’ Dichi flounders, gropes for her crutches and totters home.
sentences.zh: 哎哟！ “我需要帮助！”迪奇挣扎着，摸索着拐杖，摇摇晃晃地回家了。

sentences.en: “Ma!”
she gasps.
sentences.zh: 她喘息着。

sentences.en: Ma rushes out to wrap protective arms about her as she crumbles like charred wood in a bonfire.
sentences.zh: 当她像篝火中烧焦的木头一样崩溃时，妈妈冲出去用手臂保护她。

picturePages.text: “Ma! My ash! The – the – They’re –– cutting it!” “Who, child? Talk slowly.

sentences.en: “Ma!
My ash!
sentences.zh: 我的灰！

sentences.en: The – the – They’re –– cutting it!”
sentences.zh: 那——那——他们正在——砍它！”

sentences.en: “Who, child?
sentences.zh: “谁，孩子？

sentences.en: Talk slowly.
sentences.zh: 慢慢说。

picturePages.text: Here – drink this water.” “They c–came in a big bus with axes! So many men. Huge men with sharp axes, Ma!” “Oh no!

sentences.en: Here – drink this water.”
sentences.zh: 来——喝这水。”

sentences.en: “They c–came in a big bus with axes!
sentences.zh: “他们——带着斧子坐着一辆大巴士来了！

sentences.en: So many men.
sentences.zh: 这么多男人。

sentences.en: Huge men with sharp axes, Ma!”
sentences.zh: 巨大的男人，拿着锋利的斧子，妈妈！”

sentences.en: “Oh no!
sentences.zh: “哦不！

picturePages.text: It’s the contractor’s men come to chop our trees! Quick! We have to do something.” “You wait here.

sentences.en: It’s the contractor’s men come to chop our trees!
sentences.zh: 是承包商的人来砍我们的树！

sentences.en: Quick!
sentences.zh: 快点！

sentences.en: We have to do something.”
sentences.zh: 我们必须做点什么。”

sentences.en: “You wait here.
sentences.zh: “你在这里等着。

picturePages.text: I’ll gather everyone,” says Dichi catching her breath and squaring her shoulders. Women and children rush to rally around with dholaks. “We’ve got to do something. Contractor Chand tricked our menfolk into going away!” Ma says, wringing the edge of her phantu.

sentences.en: I’ll gather everyone,” says Dichi catching her breath and squaring her shoulders.
sentences.zh: 我会召集所有人。”迪奇喘着气，挺起肩膀说道。

sentences.en: Women and children rush to rally around with dholaks.
sentences.zh: 妇女和儿童争先恐后地聚集在多拉克周围。

sentences.en: “We’ve got to do something.
sentences.zh: “我们必须做点什么。

sentences.en: Contractor Chand tricked our menfolk into going away!”
sentences.zh: 承包商钱德骗我们的人走了！”

sentences.en: Ma says, wringing the edge of her phantu.
sentences.zh: 妈妈一边说，一边拧着法图的边缘。

picturePages.text: “How do we stop them without our menfolk?” “We’ll show them!

sentences.en: “How do we stop them without our menfolk?”
sentences.zh: “没有我们的男人，我们如何阻止他们？”

sentences.en: “We’ll show them!
sentences.zh: “我们会展示给他们看！

picturePages.text: But remember – absolutely no violence,” says the village elder, Gauri who is Ma’s best friend. Dichi’s heart booms along with her dholak.

sentences.en: But remember – absolutely no violence,” says the village elder, Gauri who is Ma’s best friend.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，绝对不能使用暴力。”村长高里（Gauri）说道，他是马云最好的朋友。

sentences.en: Dichi’s heart booms along with her dholak.
sentences.zh: 迪奇的心随着她的多拉克一起跳动。

picturePages.text: Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom! “Chipko!”

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom!
sentences.zh: 哎哟！

sentences.en: “Chipko!”
sentences.zh: “奇普科！”

picturePages.text: she yells. “Hug the trees!” holler the women and children till their throats ache for a drink of hot buttered tea.

sentences.en: she yells.
sentences.zh: 她喊道。

sentences.en: “Hug the trees!”
sentences.zh: “拥抱树木！”

sentences.en: holler the women and children till their throats ache for a drink of hot buttered tea.
sentences.zh: 喊着妇女儿童喝热酥油茶，嗓子疼。

picturePages.text: The forest throbs with the wails of chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. “What do the forests bear?” shouts Dichi, raising her fist high. “Soil, water and pure air!” chorus the women and children.

sentences.en: The forest throbs with the wails of chir, pine, deodar and ash trees.
sentences.zh: 森林里充满了赤松树、松树、雪松树和白蜡树的哀嚎。

sentences.en: “What do the forests bear?”
sentences.zh: “森林里有什么？”

sentences.en: shouts Dichi, raising her fist high.
sentences.zh: 迪奇高举拳头喊道。

sentences.en: “Soil, water and pure air!”
sentences.zh: “土壤、水和纯净的空气！”

sentences.en: chorus the women and children.
sentences.zh: 妇女和儿童合唱。

picturePages.text: The X that marks every tree to be cut, feels like a gash – a wound that will never heal. My Ash!

sentences.en: The X that marks every tree to be cut, feels like a gash – a wound that will never heal.
sentences.zh: 标记每棵要砍伐的树的 X 感觉就像一道伤口——一个永远无法愈合的伤口。

sentences.en: My Ash!
sentences.zh: 我的阿什！

picturePages.text: What will I do without you? Dichi’s trembling fingers scratch at the bark to erase the X. “You can’t cut my ash,” she says fiercely, her arms wrapped around her tree. “Move out,” rasps Contractor Chand, pulling her away roughly.

sentences.en: What will I do without you?
sentences.zh: 没有你我该怎么办？

sentences.en: Dichi’s trembling fingers scratch at the bark to erase the X.
sentences.zh: 迪奇颤抖的手指在树皮上刮擦，抹掉了X。

sentences.en: “You can’t cut my ash,” she says fiercely, her arms wrapped around her tree.
sentences.zh: “你不能砍掉我的骨灰，”她用双臂抱住树，恶狠狠地说。

sentences.en: “Move out,” rasps Contractor Chand, pulling her away roughly.
sentences.zh: “搬出去，”承包商钱德粗声粗气地把她拉开。

picturePages.text: Dichi whirls to stamp her feet. Her eagle eyes scrutinize the axemen who crowd around. They look tired and wary.

sentences.en: Dichi whirls to stamp her feet.
sentences.zh: 迪奇转过身来跺脚。

sentences.en: Her eagle eyes scrutinize the axemen who crowd around.
sentences.zh: 她鹰般的眼睛审视着周围的斧兵。

sentences.en: They look tired and wary.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来疲倦而警惕。

picturePages.text: As her gaze fixes on one figure hiding behind a tree, his eyes drop to the ground. Dichi’s eyes widen, “Chacha – you too?”

sentences.en: As her gaze fixes on one figure hiding behind a tree, his eyes drop to the ground.
sentences.zh: 当她的目光落在树后的一个人影上时，他的目光落在了地上。

sentences.en: Dichi’s eyes widen, “Chacha – you too?”
sentences.zh: 蒂奇瞪大了眼睛，“茶茶——你也是？”

picturePages.text: There’s a hush in the woods. Chacha slumps to drop his axe with a clink. “I have a gambling debt. I am out of work...” says Chacha lamely.

sentences.en: There’s a hush in the woods.
sentences.zh: 树林里一片寂静。

sentences.en: Chacha slumps to drop his axe with a clink.
sentences.zh: 茶茶倒地一声，手中的斧头掉了下来。

sentences.en: “I have a gambling debt.
sentences.zh: “我欠下了赌债。

sentences.en: I am out of work...”
sentences.zh: 我失业了……”

sentences.en: says Chacha lamely.
sentences.zh: 茶茶有气无力地说。

picturePages.text: Dichi and her brothers rush to hug him.

sentences.en: Dichi and her brothers rush to hug him.
sentences.zh: 迪奇和她的兄弟们冲过去拥抱他。

picturePages.text: “Chacha, we’ll work and help you repay your debts! I can weave a shawl and sell it!” says Dichi. “I’ll work at the soap unit,” says Ram. “I’ll work at the water mill!”

sentences.en: “Chacha, we’ll work and help you repay your debts!
sentences.zh: “茶茶，我们会努力帮你还债的！

sentences.en: I can weave a shawl and sell it!”
sentences.zh: 我可以织一条披肩然后卖掉！”

sentences.en: says Dichi.
sentences.zh: 迪奇说。

sentences.en: “I’ll work at the soap unit,” says Ram.
sentences.zh: “我将在肥皂部门工作，”拉姆说。

sentences.en: “I’ll work at the water mill!”
sentences.zh: “我要去水磨坊工作！”

picturePages.text: says Shyam. Chacha’s head droops, a teardrop glistens in his eye. He throws off the shirt of his uniform, picks up Dichi’s dholak. Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka!

sentences.en: says Shyam.
sentences.zh: 夏姆说。

sentences.en: Chacha’s head droops, a teardrop glistens in his eye.
sentences.zh: 茶茶低着头，眼里闪着泪光。

sentences.en: He throws off the shirt of his uniform, picks up Dichi’s dholak.
sentences.zh: 他脱下制服衬衫，捡起迪奇的多拉克。

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

picturePages.text: Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom!

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom!
sentences.zh: 哎哟！

picturePages.text: “What do the forests bear?” boom Chacha and Dichi. “Soil, water and pure air!” chorus the women and children.

sentences.en: “What do the forests bear?”
sentences.zh: “森林里有什么？”

sentences.en: boom Chacha and Dichi.
sentences.zh: 繁荣Chacha和Dichi。

sentences.en: “Soil, water and pure air!”
sentences.zh: “土壤、水和纯净的空气！”

sentences.en: chorus the women and children.
sentences.zh: 妇女和儿童合唱。

picturePages.text: “You foolish girl! These forests bear timber, resin and foreign exchange!” cuts in Contractor Chand. “MEN, chop down those trees at once! Every one of them – chir, pine, deodar and ash!”

sentences.en: “You foolish girl!
sentences.zh: “你这个傻丫头！

sentences.en: These forests bear timber, resin and foreign exchange!”
sentences.zh: 这些森林蕴藏着木材、树脂和外汇！”

sentences.en: cuts in Contractor Chand.
sentences.zh: 削减承包商Chand。

sentences.en: “MEN, chop down those trees at once!
sentences.zh: “伙计们，立即砍倒那些树！

sentences.en: Every one of them – chir, pine, deodar and ash!”
sentences.zh: 每一种——奇木、松树、雪松和白蜡木！”

picturePages.text: “No! No! No! Pleeeease don’t!” says Dichi holding on to her tree.

sentences.en: “No!
No!
sentences.zh: 不！

sentences.en: No!
sentences.zh: 不！

sentences.en: Pleeeease don’t!”
sentences.zh: 请不要！”

sentences.en: says Dichi holding on to her tree.
sentences.zh: 迪奇扶着她的树说道。

picturePages.text: “The trees are our saviours!” “She’s right,” says Chacha. “She lost her Dada in that flood.”

sentences.en: “The trees are our saviours!”
sentences.zh: “树木是我们的救星！”

sentences.en: “She’s right,” says Chacha.
sentences.zh: “她是对的，”恰恰说。

sentences.en: “She lost her Dada in that flood.”
sentences.zh: “她在那场洪水中失去了她的爸爸。”

picturePages.text: An axeman opens burning palms to drop his axe. Another axe clinks down and another... until one by one the axemen troop out of the forest.

sentences.en: An axeman opens burning palms to drop his axe.
sentences.zh: 一名斧头手张开燃烧的手掌，扔下了他的斧头。

sentences.en: Another axe clinks down and another... until one by one the axemen troop out of the forest.
sentences.zh: 又一把斧子叮当作响，又一把……直到斧兵们一一走出森林。

picturePages.text: Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom Dadaka! Dhoom! “Chipko!

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom Dadaka!
sentences.zh: 杜姆·达达卡！

sentences.en: Dhoom!
sentences.zh: 哎哟！

sentences.en: “Chipko!
sentences.zh: “奇普科！

picturePages.text: Hug the trees!” cries Dichi. Hoarse voices echo with the wind that whines through the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees. “Cut this forest and you’ll wipe out our village,” says Ma. A bulky form blots out the sky.

sentences.en: Hug the trees!”
sentences.zh: 拥抱树木吧！”

sentences.en: cries Dichi.
sentences.zh: 迪奇喊道。

sentences.en: Hoarse voices echo with the wind that whines through the chir, pine, deodar and ash trees.
sentences.zh: 沙哑的声音在风中回荡，呼啸着穿过桧树、松树、雪松树和白蜡树。

sentences.en: “Cut this forest and you’ll wipe out our village,” says Ma.
sentences.zh: “砍伐这片森林，你就会消灭我们的村庄，”马说。

sentences.en: A bulky form blots out the sky.
sentences.zh: 一个庞大的身影遮蔽了天空。

picturePages.text: Contractor Chand towers before them, looking like thunder.

sentences.en: Contractor Chand towers before them, looking like thunder.
sentences.zh: 承包商昌德耸立在他们面前，看上去如雷霆一般。

picturePages.text: Shaking an angry fist, he stamps his feet, turns on his heel and marches away.

sentences.en: Shaking an angry fist, he stamps his feet, turns on his heel and marches away.
sentences.zh: 他愤怒地挥舞着拳头，跺着脚，转身大步走开。

picturePages.text: Squeezing her hands together, Dichi takes a deep breath. She can’t believe it – all the axemen have gone! “We did it!” says Ma. “We’ll take our Chipko Movement to every part of India.”

sentences.en: Squeezing her hands together, Dichi takes a deep breath.
sentences.zh: 迪奇握紧双手，深吸了一口气。

sentences.en: She can’t believe it – all the axemen have gone!
sentences.zh: 她简直不敢相信——所有的斧头手都走了！

sentences.en: “We did it!”
sentences.zh: “我们做到了！”

sentences.en: says Ma.
sentences.zh: 妈妈说。

sentences.en: “We’ll take our Chipko Movement to every part of India.”
sentences.zh: “我们将把我们的 Chipko 运动带到印度的每个地方。”

picturePages.text: “Chipko! Hug the trees!” cry the women and children. Toes tap, feet thump. Hand in hand, they swing into a joyous victory dance.

sentences.en: “Chipko!
sentences.zh: “奇普科！

sentences.en: Hug the trees!”
sentences.zh: 拥抱树木吧！”

sentences.en: cry the women and children.
sentences.zh: 妇女和儿童都哭了。

sentences.en: Toes tap, feet thump.
sentences.zh: 脚趾轻敲，双脚重击。

sentences.en: Hand in hand, they swing into a joyous victory dance.
sentences.zh: 他们手拉着手，跳起了欢乐的胜利之舞。

picturePages.text: The ash sways in the breeze. Dichi rests her cheek against its cool bark. She feels its feathery leaves rustle in the evening breeze. “I’m like you, strong and fierce like a Yeti...sturdy as a yak,” Dichi whispers to her ash tree.

sentences.en: The ash sways in the breeze.
sentences.zh: 灰烬在微风中摇曳。

sentences.en: Dichi rests her cheek against its cool bark.
sentences.zh: 迪奇把脸颊靠在冰凉的树皮上。

sentences.en: She feels its feathery leaves rustle in the evening breeze.
sentences.zh: 她感觉到羽毛般的叶子在晚风中沙沙作响。

sentences.en: “I’m like you, strong and fierce like a Yeti...sturdy as a yak,” Dichi whispers to her ash tree.
sentences.zh: “我和你一样，像雪人一样坚强、凶猛……像牦牛一样坚固，”迪奇对她的白蜡树低声说道。

picturePages.text: Glossary Chacha - Uncle Chipko - To stick to, hug Dada - Father Dholak - Drum Ma - Mother Phantu - Bhotiya tribal women wear this shawl on the head tucked behind to make two pockets.

sentences.en: Glossary Chacha - Uncle Chipko - To stick to, hug Dada - Father Dholak - Drum Ma - Mother Phantu - Bhotiya tribal women wear this shawl on the head tucked behind to make two pockets.
sentences.zh: 词汇 Chacha - Chipko 叔叔 - 坚持、拥抱 Dada - 父亲 Dholak - Drum Ma - 母亲 Phantu - Bhotiya 部落妇女将这款披肩戴在头上，塞在后面，做成两个口袋。

picturePages.text: Yak - Long-haired domestic cattle Yeti - An imaginary giant ape or an abominable snowman believed to live in the Himalaya mountains of Nepal and Tibet.

sentences.en: Yak - Long-haired domestic cattle Yeti - An imaginary giant ape or an abominable snowman believed to live in the Himalaya mountains of Nepal and Tibet.
sentences.zh: 牦牛 - 长毛家牛 雪人 - 一种虚构的巨猿或可憎的雪人，据信生活在尼泊尔和西藏的喜马拉雅山脉。

picturePages.text: Bibliography is a list of published reference material used by an author to write a story. Here is a short bibliography for this book: 1. The Unquiet Woods by Ramachandra Guha 2. Chandi Prasad Bhatt, Gaura Devi, and the Chipko Movement by Mark Shepard 3.

sentences.en: Bibliography is a list of published reference material used by an author to write a story.
sentences.zh: 参考书目是作者用来撰写故事的已出版参考材料的列表。

sentences.en: Here is a short bibliography for this book: 1.
sentences.zh: 以下是本书的简短参考书目：1.

sentences.en: The Unquiet Woods by Ramachandra Guha 2.
sentences.zh: 《不安静的森林》作者：Ramachandra Guha 2。

sentences.en: Chandi Prasad Bhatt, Gaura Devi, and the Chipko Movement by Mark Shepard 3.
sentences.zh: 马克·谢泼德 (Mark Shepard) 的昌迪·普拉萨德·巴特 (Chandi Prasad Bhatt)、高拉·德维 (Gaura Devi) 和奇普科运动 (Chipko Movement) 3。

sentences.zh: 《Bhotiyas 及其邻居》作者：E C M Browne 4. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tcwY04s_mlM&feature=lated - CNN IBN – Chandi Prasad Bhatt 5. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GXnAcTS8Ais&feature=linked - Nanda Devi Campaign Bali Devi Speaks

picturePages.text: “Forestry is not about trees. It is about people.” - Jack Westoby, author of The Purpose of Forests • The Bhotiya tribe live high in the Himalaya mountains of India.

sentences.en: “Forestry is not about trees.
sentences.zh: “林业的重点不是树木。

sentences.en: It is about people.”
sentences.zh: 这是关于人的。”

sentences.en: - Jack Westoby, author of The Purpose of Forests • The Bhotiya tribe live high in the Himalaya mountains of India.
sentences.zh: - Jack Westoby，《森林的目的》一书的作者 • Bhotiya 部落生活在印度喜马拉雅山脉的高处。

picturePages.text: They love and protect the forests because they depend on them for firewood, tools and building houses. • In 1970 floods occur in Alaknanda when the forests are cleared, sweeping away houses, bridges, cattle and thousands of people.

sentences.en: They love and protect the forests because they depend on them for firewood, tools and building houses. • In 1970 floods occur in Alaknanda when the forests are cleared, sweeping away houses, bridges, cattle and thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 他们热爱并保护森林，因为他们依靠森林获取柴火、工具和建造房屋。 • 1970 年，阿拉卡南达发生洪水，森林被砍伐，房屋、桥梁、牲畜和数千人被冲走。

picturePages.text: The Bhotiyas know they have to save their forests so they adopt the Chipko Movement which promotes non-violence.

sentences.en: The Bhotiyas know they have to save their forests so they adopt the Chipko Movement which promotes non-violence.
sentences.zh: 博提亚人知道他们必须拯救森林，因此他们发起了提倡非暴力的奇普科运动。

picturePages.text: An illiterate woman, Gaura Devi, a tribal leader from Chamoli District, mobilizes the women of her region to protect their forests.

sentences.en: An illiterate woman, Gaura Devi, a tribal leader from Chamoli District, mobilizes the women of her region to protect their forests.
sentences.zh: 查莫利区的部落首领、文盲妇女加乌拉·德维 (Gaura Devi) 动员该地区的妇女保护她们的森林。

picturePages.text: Some consider this an eco-feminist movement where women are actively involved. • In the Alaknanda Valley, Chandi Prasad Bhatt is a humble social worker who teaches the people to embrace the trees and save them from the axemen.

sentences.en: Some consider this an eco-feminist movement where women are actively involved. • In the Alaknanda Valley, Chandi Prasad Bhatt is a humble social worker who teaches the people to embrace the trees and save them from the axemen.
sentences.zh: 一些人认为这是一场女性积极参与的生态女权主义运动。 • 在阿拉卡南达山谷，昌迪·普拉萨德·巴特 (Chandi Prasad Bhatt) 是一位谦虚的社会工作者，他教导人们拥抱树木并将它们从斧头手中拯救出来。

picturePages.text: Like Mahatma Gandhi, he doesn’t use violence. He encourages tribals to develop their local industries without disturbing the forest wealth. • “Ecology is permanent economy,” says Chipko leader, Sunderlal Bahuguna, who continues the movement to fight the felling of forests.

sentences.en: Like Mahatma Gandhi, he doesn’t use violence.
sentences.zh: 像圣雄甘地一样，他不使用暴力。

sentences.en: He encourages tribals to develop their local industries without disturbing the forest wealth. • “Ecology is permanent economy,” says Chipko leader, Sunderlal Bahuguna, who continues the movement to fight the felling of forests.
sentences.zh: 他鼓励部落在不破坏森林财富的情况下发展当地工业。 • “生态是永久经济”，Chipko 领导人 Sunderlal Bahuguna 说道，他继续开展反对砍伐森林的运动。

picturePages.text: • Like Dichi in this book, a little Bhotiya girl spots the axemen and alerts the village women who march into the forest with shouts of Chipko slogans.

sentences.en: • Like Dichi in this book, a little Bhotiya girl spots the axemen and alerts the village women who march into the forest with shouts of Chipko slogans.
sentences.zh: • 就像本书中的迪奇一样，一位博提亚小女孩发现了斧头手，并用奇普科口号的喊声提醒走进森林的村里妇女。

picturePages.text: Without violence, they block the axemen from cutting the trees. • In 1980, the Government of India passes a law to protect these forests.

sentences.en: Without violence, they block the axemen from cutting the trees. • In 1980, the Government of India passes a law to protect these forests.
sentences.zh: 他们没有使用暴力，阻止了斧头砍伐树木。 • 1980 年，印度政府通过了一项保护这些森林的法律。

picturePages.text: This is one of the first important environmental movements in India.

sentences.en: This is one of the first important environmental movements in India.
sentences.zh: 这是印度最早的重要环保运动之一。
